The thing with MLS is that it basically requires a central server for ordering the commits. For Matrix' interpretation of federation, this doesn't really work because a group isn't really owned by a server, it is a DAG of events, which, as is the nature of DAGs, does not have the total order needed for MLS commit ordering.

So either you introduce a central party that does ordering, or you do BFT-style consensus, or you try to get some idea of branching an merging of group states into MLS, which isn't really possible with what RFC 9420 offers.

My impression also is that the Matrix community really loves their DAGs and the group state management that they built, and from an MLS perspective it makes more sense to store that in the group context (either as extensions or as components as defined in draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10).

There is draft-xue-mls-decentralized which proposes two ways to MLS offer some foundations, one of which (IMO) only solves half the problem and the other (IMO) doesn't make sense.
